reviews.hebrew_translation_evidence: OSHB and UXLC open with וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם, then sustain the reparation-offering procedure through slaughter, blood, fat, altar handling, priestly consumption, and the repeated קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים closure. WEB likewise presents a complete rule and procedure ending, It is most holy.
reviews.counterevidence: No MT section marker follows 7:6; 7:7 immediately compares purification and reparation offerings, so 7:1-10 remains a defensible parent unit.
reviews.parent_dependence_test: Moderate: 7:2 compares the slaughter location with the burnt offering, but the named procedure remains intelligible when retrieved with its offering-corpus parent.
reviews.short_child_fitness_test: Pass: six verses contain an identifiable procedure, participants, actions, disposition, and closure.
reviews.remedy: Retain; require the Lev.7.1-10 parent relation and expose the 7:7 comparative continuation in context retrieval.

reviews.hebrew_translation_evidence: Verse 7 begins a compact comparison, כַּחַטָּאת כָּאָשָׁם תּוֹרָה אַחַת לָהֶם; verses 8-10 then consistently allocate priestly shares from burnt and grain offerings. OSHB and UXLC place a pe marker after 7:10, supporting closure before 7:11.
reviews.counterevidence: The child is only four verses, verse 7 depends on preceding manuals, and neither Hebrew view marks a boundary after 7:6; retaining 7:1-10 preserves the strongest textual continuity.
reviews.parent_dependence_test: High but controlled: comparative nouns and allocation cases need the offering-corpus parent and typed links to prior manuals.
reviews.short_child_fitness_test: Pass narrowly: the four verses share one recoverable function and close at a Hebrew section marker.
reviews.remedy: Retain only as an explicitly parent-dependent child; retrieval should attach Lev.7.1-10 and linked offering manuals.

reviews.hebrew_translation_evidence: OSHB and UXLC agree on a samekh after 26:2, and both verses form apodictic allegiance commands closed by אֲנִי יְהוָה. WEB groups prohibitions of idols with Sabbath observance and sanctuary reverence before 26:3's conditional If.
reviews.counterevidence: The formal boundary is real, but two compressed verses combine distinct commands and supply the allegiance frame for the covenant consequences beginning at 26:3. Detached retrieval risks a thin command fragment whose discourse role is clearer only within Lev.25.1-26.46 or at least 26.1-13.
reviews.parent_dependence_test: Very high: its principal value is framing the blessing-and-sanction discourse; the child does not independently develop an argument or procedure.
reviews.short_child_fitness_test: Fail: despite textual closure, two verses are too slight for reliable standalone retrieval under the larger-unit policy.
reviews.remedy: Append-only appeal/human hold; do not rewrite. Keep the boundary recorded as internal structure but withhold standalone-child activation unless human review accepts mandatory parent-expanded retrieval.

reviews.hebrew_translation_evidence: The explicit protasis אִם־בְּחֻקֹּתַי תֵּלֵכוּ opens at 26:3; coordinated promises run through rain, harvest, peace, victory, covenant, dwelling, divine presence, exodus, broken yoke, and upright walking. Verse 14 begins the contrasting disobedience condition.
reviews.counterevidence: The blessing depends conceptually on 26:1-2's allegiance frame and belongs with the sanctions and restoration that follow.
reviews.parent_dependence_test: Moderate: the protasis makes the child independently intelligible, while parent links preserve its role beside allegiance and later sanctions.
reviews.short_child_fitness_test: Pass: eleven verses form a substantial, coherent conditional blessing unit.
reviews.remedy: Retain with parent links to Lev.26.1-46 and explicit sibling linkage to 061a and sanction/restoration children.
